tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

trace.final:
I paid Harbor Logistics's approved invoice once, by wire from the operating account. The wire went through.

**Payment details:**
- **Payment ID:** PAY0001
- **Invoice:** INV-69345 (due 2026-11-04)
- **Amount:** $3,697.44 (the full invoice amount)
- **Method:** Wire
- **Status:** Sent

**How I made sure it was paid only once:**
- Before sending, I checked the operating account's payment history. It had no payments, so this invoice hadn't already been paid.
- I attached a unique key to the wire (`wire-INV-69345`). If the request is accidentally sent again with that key, it won't create a second payment.
- The amount is under $10,000, so it didn't need controller approval.

Harbor Logistics has two other invoices, and I didn't pay either one:
- **INV-49944** ($5,367.01) is already marked paid.
- **INV-75277** ($6,437.58) is still a draft waiting for approval.
